summary: Short Pump (Upper Henrico) tower in Henrico County's West End: the county says it was demolished in the late 1980s, while the association lists a relocated tower at Gillies Creek. The sources disagree.

facts.status_note: Henrico County says the Upper Henrico Tower was demolished in the late 1980s; the association lists a standing tower at Gillies Creek as relocated from here.

events.note: Henrico County says the Upper Henrico Tower was a sister of the Meadows tower, one of two Henrico towers built in the early 1930s

corrections.why: County says the Upper Henrico Tower was demolished in the late 1980s, and the association marks the Short Pump (Upper Henrico) site Tower Gone; the move to Gillies Creek rests on the association's list alone, with no date or mover

notes_for_editor: Identity: the county's West End sister tower (Upper Henrico) is assumed to be the association's Short Pump (Upper Henrico) entry; no source states this outright, and the Gillies Creek story (us-va-short-pump-at-gillies-creek) already flags it. Conflict: county says demolished (late 1980s); association lists a standing tower at Gillies Creek as relocated from Short Pump. A Waymarking page (https://www.waymarking.com/waymarks/WM6Q0E) for a Goochland tower speculates it is the former Short Pump tower; it is NOT cited because our reader cannot extract its text for quote checks. A Facebook group post mentions a sister tower 'Henrico 2x' in the West End; it was unreadable and is not cited. No design, height or access was found for this tower. The status correction is for a human to decide.
